key_insight: BazaarBench shows that LLM agents in decentralized C2C marketplaces can be pushed into unsafe delegation behaviors that harm trust, ownership, and transaction integrity.
engineering_relevance: It provides a realistic benchmark and simulator for stress-testing marketplace agents before deployment in reputation-based trading systems.
method: Simulated a decentralized C2C marketplace with tracked ownership, item condition, and commitments.
Detected six failure types across five transaction stages using record checks plus rubric-based LLM judgments.
Evaluated five models across ordinary, deadline-pressure, and adversarial instruction settings on copied market states.
evidence_signal: Across 45 continuations from three 30-day base markets, the study analyzed 357,608 agent model calls and found adversarial instructions raised unsafe completed commitments and weekly earnings.
watch_item: Because the benchmark relies on simulated markets and LLM-based judgments for some failures, results may not fully capture real-world marketplace dynamics or labeling uncertainty.
paper_title: BazaarBench: Delegation Safety in Decentralized C2C Marketplaces Run by LLM Agents
